name.text: Finding the mistake in a binomial approximation

questiontext.text:
Njeri used the expansion of \((1 + x)^{@n@}\) to estimate \({@Nd@}^{@n@}\) correct to 4 decimal places. Her working has one mistake.

  1. \({@Nd@} = 1 + x\) with \(x = -{@dd@}\).
  2. The row for power \({@n@}\) starts \(1, {@cs[1]@}, {@cs[2]@}, {@cs[3]@}\).
  3. \(x^2 = {@x2d@}\), \(x^3 = {@x3d@}\).
  4. The first four terms are \(1, {@ttd[1]@}, {@ttd[2]@}, {@ttd[3]@}\).
  5. Their sum is \({@Sd@}\).
  6. So \({@Nd@}^{@n@} \approx {@Rd@}\).

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct value of \({@Nd@}^{@n@}\), correct to 4 decimal places.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Check each step: the row of Pascal's triangle, the powers of \(x\) (a square has twice as many decimal places as the number), and the sign of each term (odd powers of a negative number are negative).

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 2: \(1, {@cs[1]@}, {@cs[2]@}, {@cs[3]@}\) starts the row for power \({@n-1@}\). The row for power \({@n@}\) starts \(1, {@C1@}, {@C2@}, {@C3@}\).

[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 3: \(({@dd@})^2\) has twice as many decimal places as \({@dd@}\), so \(x^2 = {@cx2@}\) and \(x^3 = {@cx3@}\).

[[else]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 4: \(x^3\) is negative, so the fourth term is \({@ct[3]@}\), not \({@ttd[3]@}\).

[[/if]]

(b) Done correctly: \(x = -{@dd@}\), the row starts \(1, {@C1@}, {@C2@}, {@C3@}\), \(x^2 = {@cx2@}\), \(x^3 = {@cx3@}\), the terms are \(1, {@ct[1]@}, {@ct[2]@}, {@ct[3]@}\), their sum is \({@S4d@}\), so \({@Nd@}^{@n@} \approx {@R4@}\).

questionnote.text: ix={@ix@}, n={@n@}, d={@dd@}, er={@er@}, shown {@Rd@}, correct {@R4@}

Binomial Expansions: finding the mistake in a binomial approximation

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.2: Find the wrong step in a worked four-term estimate of (1 - d)^n and give the correct value to 4 decimal places.
